newsitem.title: USA: Girl drowns as flash flooding hits central Texas.
newsitem.headline: Girl drowns as flash flooding hits central Texas.

text.p: A teenage girl was swept away and drowned in a raging creek Tuesday as heavy rains produced flash flooding across parts of central Texas, officials said.
The 17-year old girl, out for a morning walk in the rain with two friends, slipped into the creek swollen by up to 10 inches of rain that fell over the past four days in some areas around Austin.

"She stepped on a pile of debris she thought was firm ground, her friends said. The water was lapping up over the sidewalk and it swept her in," Austin Fire Department spokeswoman Cathy Brandewie said.
Flash flood warnings were issued across central and southeast Texas and the National Weather Service said two more inches of rain were expected to fall in the Austin area Tuesday.

Lowland flooding was reported along sections of the Colorado River, which crested downriver from Austin in Bastrop at 22 feet, slightly below flood stage but the river's highest level there since December 1991.

Upriver in Hays County, 51 condominium apartments were flooded and 43 cars and one boat damaged after rain-swollen tributaries overflowed their banks on Monday, emergency coordinator A.D. Carroll said.
